title: A finite integral cover of a normal integral scheme has a sheaf norm
statement:
Let $p:Y	o Z$ be a finite surjective morphism of integral schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Suppose each local ring of $Z$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. There are an integer $d\geq1$ and maps $
u_V:\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)	o\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$ for all open $V\subseteq Z$, compatible with restriction and preserving multiplication and $1$, such that $
u_V(p^\sharp a)=a^d$ for every $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$, and $b(y)=0$ implies $
u_V(b)(p(y))=0$ for every $b\in\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $y\in p^{-1}V$. Here values at points are taken in their residue fields [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case); the norm of positive degree is defined in Section 0BCX (divisors-section-norms), conditions (1) and (2).

proof.text: For a nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Z$, write $p^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Finiteness supplies this affine inverse image and makes $A$ a finite $B$-module. Surjectivity makes it nonempty, and integrality of the schemes makes $A,B$ domains. The map $B\to A$ is injective: a point above the prime $(0)\subset B$ exists by surjectivity, its prime in $A$ contracts to zero, and the kernel is contained in that contraction. Thus the fraction fields form a finite extension by the cited finite-domain lemma. These fields identify with the generic stalks $K=k(Y)$ and $L=k(Z)$ by the affine-fraction-field lemma. The map $p$ sends the generic point of $Y$ to that of $Z$: its image is dense since $p$ is continuous and surjective. The fraction-field embeddings on every affine are therefore the same map $L\hookrightarrow K$ on generic stalks, because they extend the same section maps and fractions have a unique extension. Fix $d=\dim_L K\geq1$; it is independent of the affine open.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), first paragraph, affine rings and their fraction fields

proof.text: The affine ring $B$ is integrally closed in $L$. Indeed, if $c\in L$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $B$, that polynomial maps to a monic polynomial over each $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $z\in U$. The stalk embeds in $L$ and has $L$ as fraction field, so normality of that stalk puts $c$ in its image. The cited section-gluing statement then supplies $b\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Z)=B$ with generic germ $c$. Hence $B$ is integrally closed, without any Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), normality needed for the application of the minimal-polynomial lemma

proof.text:
Let $N=N_{K/L}$ be the field norm. Every $a\in A$ is integral over $B$ by finite-algebra integrality. The minimal-polynomial descent lemma gives a monic $Q_a\in B[T]$, annihilating $a$ in $A$, whose image in $L[T]$ is its minimal polynomial. If $m=\deg Q_a$ and $e=\dim_{L(a)}K\geq1$, the field-norm formula says $N(a)=((-1)^mQ_a(0))^e\in B$. Define $
u_U(a)$ to be this element of $B$, equivalently the unique element with image $N(a)$ in $L$. Since the field norm preserves multiplication and one, injectivity of $B	o L$ proves the same for $
u_U$. Its scalar formula gives $
u_U(p^\sharp b)=b^d$ for $b\in B$.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), first paragraph, minimal polynomial and construction on affine sections

proof.text: If $W\subseteq U$ is another nonempty affine open, the sections $a$ and $a|_{p^{-1}W}$ have the same generic germ in $K$. Both $\nu_U(a)|_W$ and $\nu_W(a|_{p^{-1}W})$ consequently have germ $N(a)$ in $L$, so they are equal by injectivity of the germ map on $W$. For two affine opens $U,U^{\prime}$, cover $U\cap U^{\prime}$ by affine opens $W$ and apply this equality twice. Thus the affine norms agree on overlaps. This uses no assumption that the intersection itself is affine.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), compatible system of maps on affine sections

proof.text:
For any nonempty open $V\subseteq Z$ and $a\in\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)$, choose an affine cover $(U_i)$ of $V$. The sections $
u_{U_i}(a|_{p^{-1}U_i})$ agree on overlaps by the preceding step, so the structure-sheaf axiom glues them uniquely to $
u_V(a)$. Uniqueness of gluing proves compatibility with restriction to every open subset. Multiplicativity, preservation of one, and $
u_V(p^\sharp b)=b^d$ hold after restricting to every $U_i$, hence hold on $V$ by the uniqueness part of the same sheaf axiom. For $V=\varnothing$ both section rings have one element; use the unique map. This also verifies restrictions to the empty open.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), global norm map and property (1)

proof.text: For property (2), take $y\in p^{-1}V$ with $a(y)=0$, and choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq V$ of $p(y)$. Write $p^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $a_U=a|_{p^{-1}U}$. The point $y$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$, and $a_U\in\mathfrak q$ by the affine vanishing criterion. Its image point has prime $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak q\cap B$. From step 3 write $Q_{a_U}(T)=T^m+\sum_{i<m}b_iT^i$ in $B[T]$, with $Q_{a_U}(a_U)=0$. Thus $b_0=-a_U(a_U^{m-1}+\sum_{1\leq i<m}b_i a_U^{i-1})\in\mathfrak q$, so $b_0\in\mathfrak r$. The signed norm formula gives $\nu_U(a_U)=((-1)^mb_0)^e\in\mathfrak r$ since $e\geq1$. The affine vanishing criterion says this section vanishes at $p(y)$, and restriction compatibility gives $\nu_V(a)(p(y))=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), final paragraph, vanishing at the image point; constant coefficient is b_0 and the sign is retained
